newsitem.title: INDONESIA: One Timor rebel killed, 14 captured by Indonesians.
newsitem.headline: One Timor rebel killed, 14 captured by Indonesians.

text.p: One rebel was killed and 14 captured after a shoot-out between Indonesian troops and armed guerrillas resisting Jakarta's rule in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.

East Timor army chief Colonel Slamat Sidabutar was quoted as saying on Friday the guerillas were followers of David Alex, believed to have been the second in command of about 200 rebels, who died after being captured on June 25.
"We have captured 14 of about 20 (rebels) who are followers of David Alex at 0925 hours, Thursday," Sidabutar was quoted as saying.
Some Indonesian newspaper reports published on Saturday also quoted Sidabutar as saying the clash occurred on Wednesday. Army officials were not immediately available to explain the discrepancy.
Sidabutar said the army, acting on a tip from locals, surrounded a rebel hideout near Curusa village in the Baucau regency, about 130 km (80 miles) east of the capital Dili.
A shoot-out ensued and the rebels retreated to the forest . A soldier, Private First Class Rafael Dos Santos, was wounded in the clash, Sidabutar said.
Those arrested confessed to being members of Alex's group, he added.
The Indonesian military said Alex died on the operating table at the Dili military hospital on June 25. He had been shot twice after a firefight near Baucau, while five others were captured unharmed.
Family members have questioned the circumstances of his death because he was quickly buried by the military, without full notification and participation of the victim's family.

Alex was believed to have been fighting as part of Falintil, the armed wing of the East Timor pro-independence Fretilin movement, which has opposed Jakarta's rule since the 1975 invasion of the territory by Indonesian forces.
Indonesia annexed East Timor in 1976 and regards it as its 27th province. The United Nations has never recognised the move and still regards Portugal as the administering power.
The territory has been hit by the worst upsurge of violence in years after rebels sought to disrupt Indonesia's May 29 general election with a series of attacks in East Timor.

At least 37 people have died since the eve of polling day in a series of clashes, including 16 policeman and one soldier in one ambush. Police have said more than 70 have been detained over the same period.
